title: add-sample-weighted-explainers-ci-adapter
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Introduces a CI adapter that attaches sample-weighted local explainers to smokecheck/regression failures and prioritizes flaky/impactful prompt-sets for triage. Motivation: Our smokechecks surface frequent failures but lack a quick signal for which prompts contribute most to downstream quality risk. This PR augments the eval pipeline with a lightweight explainer that estimates per-sample influence (counterfactual token-saliency proxy + Monte Carlo perturbation aggregate) and a prioritizer that surfaces the top-K prompt-sets by weighted-impact score. The feature operates in two modes: offline (during nightly backfills) and fast-path in CI (on triggered regression failures) with a bounded runtime budget. Changes: - New CI adapter: eval_harness/ci/adapters/sample_weighted_explainer.py (core logic + config) - Hook integration: eval_harness/ci/hooks/impact_prioritizer_hook.py (attaches to smokecheck job) - Small metrics: eval_harness/metrics/impact_metrics.py (sample_weighted_impact, top_k_coverage) - Tests: tests/ci/test_explainer_fastpath.py and tests/metrics/test_impact_metrics.py - Docs: docs/ci/quality_gates.md (added a short section describing the adapter and how to tune budgets) - Config: ci/default_hooks.yaml updated to include prioritizer with conservative defaults Compatibility: The adapter is opt-in in CI via an env flag EVAL_EXPLAINER_ENABLED and bounded by MAX_EXPLAINER_SECONDS. Default run in PR CI is disabled; enabled in nightly/regression pipelines and for manual triage runs. Performance: Fast-path mode samples N=32 perturbed completions and uses token-saliency heuristics to approximate influence; wall-time budget for fast-path is 6s per prompt-set in CI. Motivation doc and microbenchmarks in the PR description show median extra CI time of ~1.8s per failure when fast-path is enabled, and ~18s in nightly full-mode. Safety and cost: explainers do not store model outputs beyond ephemeral evaluation logs and respect data retention policies. There are knobs for on/off, sample size, and a fallback to a cheap heuristic when budget is exceeded. Related: Linked to ENG-2097 (priority triage for prompt regressions) and ENG-2275 (smokecheck failure taxonomy); follows design notes in docs/ci/arch/impact-triage.md.
